messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Alert: vpc-eu-west-1 / tenant=lumen — sudden prefix KV hit-rate drop detected (from ~92% to 8%) across dedicated pool cedar-prod-3. Autoscaling and latencies degraded. Pager triggered.
Elaine (oncall-sre): Thanks — I'm on it. Paging Jay and Anton. Can someone confirm scope: only lumen tenant or other tenants on cedar-prod-3? :eyes:
Jay (eng-runtime): Checking now. Seen a spike in KV misses and prefetch evictions tied to a small set of hot prefixes from lumen. Looks like cache pollution: their traffic pattern started sending high-cardinality prefixes (long randomized ids).
Anton (eng-ml): If those prefixes are new it could bypass our prefix compression heuristics. If tenant mixing allowed same pool, other tenants will see pressure. Do we have per-tenant cache isolation metrics?
Miguel (platform-ops): We do in metrics but not enforced isolation here (dedicated pool still shares cache structures). Dashboard: https://grafana/redwood/d/cedar-prod-3?orgId=1 — hit-rate panel shows lumen spike 21:07 UTC.
Amaia (acct-mgr): Lumen's SRE (LumenOps) just replied to my ping, they're seeing increased 500s and higher P95. They've opened a ticket. I told them we're investigating.
LumenOps (customer): Confirming — started after a deploy on their side ~20:58 UTC. They rolled out a feature that fans out lookups. We can throttle on our side if needed.
Elaine (oncall-sre): Immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) throttle lumen's max concurrency at proxy 2) disable tenant prefetch/prefix caching for lumen 3) apply eviction whitelist/denylist to stop pollution. Which is lowest-risk to do now?
Jay (eng-runtime): Lowest risk: flip tenant-level prefix prefetch off and enable aggressive per-tenant TTL for their prefixes. Command to toggle (internal):
```
# disable prefetch for tenant lumen
redwoodctl tenant update --id lumen --prefetch enabled=false
# set prefix TTL to 30s
redwoodctl tenant update --id lumen --kv-prefix-ttl 30s
```
I'll run those if Elaine ok.
Elaine (oncall-sre): Do it. Also push a temporary route to fallback model-vsmall for that tenant to reduce KV pressure.
Jay (eng-runtime): Executing now. 
```
> redwoodctl tenant update --id lumen --prefetch enabled=false
> OK: prefetch disabled
> redwoodctl tenant update --id lumen --kv-prefix-ttl 30s
> OK: kv-prefix-ttl updated
> route update lumen --model fallback-vsmall --immediate
> OK: routing rule applied
```
Elaine (oncall-sre): Observability — Miguel, can you watch KV hit-rate and latencies for next 10m and confirm if there's uplift?
Miguel (platform-ops): Watching. Initial: miss rate dropped from 92%->58% miss to ~20% now. P95 latency for cedar-prod-3 improved from 870ms -> 320ms within 2m.
Anton (eng-ml): Note: switching to fallback-vsmall will change output quality. We must mark this as a fidelity mitigation and notify product + customer.
Amaia (acct-mgr): I'll message the customer channel: short note explaining temporary mitigation and fidelity tradeoff.
LumenOps (customer): Thanks. We can also start rolling back our deploy if you recommend it — we can hold traffic.
Elaine (oncall-sre): For now keep their deploy but keep prefetch disabled. If we see recurrent pollution, we'll need to gate their deployment or suggest prefix normalization.
PagerDuty: Reminder: oncall rotation for SRE handoff at 2149010800 UTC. Elaine please acknowledge final state before handoff.
Elaine (oncall-sre): Acknowledged. Current status: prefetch disabled, TTL shortened, fallback routing active. Metrics improving; customer aware. Escalation path: if hit-rate rebounds >30% miss or P95 >600ms for 5m, re-open page and escalate to infra-leads.
Jay (eng-runtime): Suggest a longer-term: add tenant-scoped LRU sharding and a per-tenant prefetch budget to prevent single-tenant pollution. I'll spin up a proposal and a short RFC.
Anton (eng-ml): Also add a quick eval: detect high-cardinality prefix patterns and auto-disable prefetch for that tenant. Could be a fast rule.
Miguel (platform-ops): For follow-up ops: we should consider an emergency policy to isolate dedicated pools per tenant if pattern repeats.
Amaia (acct-mgr): I'll coordinate a post-incident call with Lumen's ops for root cause and remediation timeline.
LumenOps (customer): We're okay with the temporary changes. We'll look at normalizing prefixes on our end and keep you posted.
Elaine (oncall-sre): I'm going to document this in the incident tracker and set severity: Sev2 (customer-impacting but mitigated). Will hand off to Jay for longer-term engineering work at 2149010800. Good job team. :thumbsup:
Jay (eng-runtime): Copy. I'll pick up RFC and follow-ups.
IncidentBot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, severity=2, assignees=[Elaine, Jay], incident_link=https://incidents/redwood/INC-2149007777
PagerDuty: Handoff reminder: Elaine please update oncall notes before sign-off.
Elaine (oncall-sre): Notes added. Leaving oncall. Handing to Jay.
Jay (eng-runtime): Taking over. Will file action items: 1) RFC for per-tenant caching budgets 2) quick rule to detect high-cardinality prefixes 3) runbook update.
Miguel (platform-ops): I'll schedule a capacity test on cedar-prod-3 after this for safe validation.
Amaia (acct-mgr): I'll follow up with Lumen for a joint RCA meeting tomorrow.
LumenOps (customer): Appreciate the rapid response. We'll send logs of the offending deploy.
Elaine (oncall-sre): Closing slack thread. If anything regresses, reopen or ping oncall. :white_check_mark:
